title: Complete Python OOP refresher: classes, inheritance, dunder methods
description: Work through CampusX OOP lectures. Build a small BankAccount class with deposit, withdraw, and __repr__.

title: Master Python comprehensions, generators, and itertools
description: Solve 10 exercises on list/dict/set comprehensions from Exercism. Rewrite them using generator expressions and measure memory usage.

title: NumPy core: arrays, broadcasting, vectorized operations
description: Complete the official NumPy quickstart + absolute beginner guide. Solve the 100 NumPy exercises (first 30).

title: pandas fundamentals: DataFrames, indexing, filtering, groupby
description: Work through the pandas 10-minutes tutorial then solve the first 25 exercises on 101 pandas puzzles.

title: SQLBolt lessons 1–9: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER, JOINs
description: Complete SQLBolt interactive lessons 1–9. Write your own 5 queries against the provided sample data and annotate each with what it returns.

title: Set up local Jupyter environment + Chinook PostgreSQL database
description: Install JupyterLab, DBeaver, and PostgreSQL locally. Download and restore the Chinook sample database. Verify you can run queries from both DBeaver and Python via psycopg2.

title: SQLBolt lessons 10–18: GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, window functions
description: Complete SQLBolt lessons 10–18. Then write 5 window function queries (RANK, ROW_NUMBER, LAG) against the Chinook database.

title: Advanced pandas: merge, reshape, pivot tables, time-series indexing
description: Complete pandas exercises 26–60 from 101 pandas puzzles, focusing on merge/join patterns and reshaping with melt/pivot.

title: Python file I/O: CSV, JSON, Excel with pandas and openpyxl
description: Write scripts to read/write CSV, JSON, and Excel. Practice reading a multi-sheet Excel workbook and writing aggregated results back.

title: Query the Chinook DB with Python: answer 10 business questions with SQL + pandas
description: Write a Jupyter notebook with 10 business questions about the Chinook music store (top artists by revenue, monthly sales trend, customer LTV). Answer each with a SQL query via psycopg2 and visualize with a simple chart.

title: Statistics fundamentals: mean, variance, distributions, CLT in Python
description: Work through statistics concepts covering Distributions and CLT. Replicate all formulas in Python using scipy.stats and numpy.

title: Choose EDA mini-project dataset from Kaggle and write project plan
description: Browse Kaggle datasets. Pick one with 50k+ rows and real messiness (nulls, inconsistent formats). Write a 1-page markdown plan: questions to answer, expected cleaning steps, chart types you'll produce.

title: Data cleaning: handle nulls, duplicates, outliers, type coercion in pandas
description: Using your chosen Kaggle dataset, apply a full cleaning pipeline: audit nulls, drop/impute, remove duplicates, fix dtypes, cap outliers. Document each decision with a comment.

title: matplotlib mastery: line, bar, scatter, histogram, subplots, custom styles
description: Create 8 chart types using matplotlib on your EDA dataset. Apply a consistent custom style (colors, fonts, grid). Save to PNG for use in your notebook.

title: Interactive charts with plotly: scatter, bar, choropleth, and subplots
description: Recreate your 4 best matplotlib charts in plotly express. Add hover tooltips and titles. Embed the output HTML in your Jupyter notebook.

title: Hypothesis testing: t-tests, chi-square, p-values — apply to your dataset
description: Identify 2 testable hypotheses in your dataset. Run t-tests or chi-square tests using scipy.stats, interpret p-values, state conclusions clearly in markdown cells.

title: Correlation analysis and heatmaps: Pearson, Spearman, seaborn heatmap
description: Compute full correlation matrix on your dataset. Build a seaborn heatmap with annotations. Write a paragraph interpreting the 3 strongest correlations.

title: EDA notebook first draft: cleaning + 8 charts + statistical insights
description: Assemble your EDA notebook with cleaned data, all charts, hypothesis tests, and a written narrative. Push to a GitHub repo and enable GitHub Pages or share as a Kaggle notebook.

title: Excel & Google Sheets: pivot tables, VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, named ranges
description: Download the Superstore Sales Excel dataset. Build 3 pivot tables: sales by region+category, monthly trend, top 10 customers. Use INDEX/MATCH for a lookup table.

resources.title: Leila Gharani — Excel Pivot Tables & Dashboards

title: Build a Power BI dashboard: import CSV, create 4 visuals, publish to Power BI Service
description: Download Power BI Desktop (free). Import your cleaned Superstore CSV. Build a 1-page report: KPI card (total sales), bar chart (sales by category), line chart (monthly trend), and map visual (sales by region). Apply a dark theme, add slicers for year and region, then publish to Power BI Service and share the public link.

resources.title: Leila Gharani — Power BI Full Course for Beginners

title: Advanced SQL: CTEs, recursive queries, materialized views on PostgreSQL
description: Write 3 queries using CTEs on the Chinook DB. Build one recursive CTE for a hierarchy. Create a materialized view for the monthly sales summary.

resources.title: CampusX — Advanced SQL CTEs & Window Functions

title: Probability distributions deep dive: normal, Poisson, binomial with scipy
description: Model 3 real phenomena from your dataset with appropriate distributions. Plot PDF/CDF for each. Compute confidence intervals using scipy.stats.

title: Polish and publish EDA notebook: add executive summary and methodology section
description: Add an introduction cell with dataset context, a methodology section, and a conclusions cell with 5 actionable insights. Publish on Kaggle or GitHub Pages. Share the link.

title: Data Analyst path review: knowledge gaps audit + certificate progress check
description: Score yourself 1–5 on each skill in the Data Analyst path. List the 3 weakest areas. Spend remaining time reinforcing them. Check progress on Google Data Analytics certificate.

title: Month 1 Milestone: Publish EDA project + update LinkedIn with Data Analyst skills
description: Your EDA notebook must be live on Kaggle/GitHub. Update your LinkedIn with: pandas, SQL, Python, data visualization, statistical analysis. Write a 150-word LinkedIn post about what you learned.

title: scikit-learn workflow: Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, fit/predict/score pattern
description: Read the scikit-learn Getting Started guide. Build a full preprocessing Pipeline with ColumnTransformer (scaler for numeric, OneHotEncoder for categorical) on the Titanic dataset.

title: Linear & logistic regression: train, evaluate, interpret coefficients
description: Train LinearRegression on California Housing and LogisticRegression on Titanic. Plot residuals for regression. Plot confusion matrix and ROC curve for classification.

resources.title: CampusX — 100 Days of ML: Linear Regression

title: Decision trees and random forests: hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV
description: Train a DecisionTreeClassifier on Titanic, visualize the tree with graphviz. Tune max_depth and min_samples_split with GridSearchCV. Train RandomForestClassifier and compare AUC.

resources.title: CampusX — 100 Days of ML: Decision Trees & Random Forest

title: Model evaluation deep dive: precision/recall tradeoff, F1, cross-val, learning curves
description: For your Titanic classifier: plot precision-recall curve, compute F1 at 3 thresholds, run 5-fold cross-val, and plot a learning curve to diagnose bias vs variance.

resources.title: CampusX — 100 Days of ML: Model Evaluation

title: Feature engineering: binning, interaction terms, target encoding, feature importance
description: Engineer 5 new features on Titanic (title from name, family size, cabin deck). Use RandomForest feature_importances_ to rank them. Verify improvements in cross-val AUC.

resources.title: CampusX — 100 Days of ML: Feature Engineering

title: Choose and set up ML mini-project dataset + problem definition
description: Pick a Kaggle dataset suitable for an end-to-end ML project (classification or regression, 10k+ rows). Write a problem statement: business question, success metric, baseline model.

title: K-means and DBSCAN clustering: choose k with elbow method, evaluate with silhouette score
description: Apply K-means to the Mall Customer Segmentation dataset. Use the elbow method and silhouette score to choose k. Apply DBSCAN and compare cluster shapes. Visualize with PCA 2D.

title: PCA and dimensionality reduction: reduce to 2D, explain variance, apply to MNIST subset
description: Apply PCA to MNIST (10k samples). Plot explained variance curve. Reduce to 2D and visualize digit clusters. Compare with UMAP on the same data.

title: Gradient boosting: XGBoost vs LightGBM on your mini-project dataset
description: Train XGBoost and LightGBM on your ML project dataset. Tune n_estimators and learning_rate with RandomizedSearchCV. Compare against your baseline RandomForest.

resources.title: CampusX — 100 Days of ML: Gradient Boosting & XGBoost

title: SHAP values: interpret your best model's predictions with force plots and summary plots
description: Install shap. Apply TreeExplainer to your best model. Generate a summary plot, a force plot for 3 individual predictions, and a dependence plot for the top feature.

title: Build end-to-end ML pipeline: ingest → clean → features → train → evaluate → save model
description: Write a single train.py script that runs your full pipeline for your ML project. Save the trained model with joblib. Write a predict.py that loads it and scores new rows from a CSV.

title: ML mini-project: trained model + evaluation report in Jupyter notebook
description: Assemble your ML project notebook: data description, EDA, preprocessing, model comparison table, best model metrics, SHAP interpretations, and next steps. Push to GitHub.

title: PyTorch fundamentals: tensors, autograd, and a manual linear regression
description: Complete the official PyTorch 60-minute blitz tutorial. Implement linear regression manually (no nn.Module): forward pass, MSE loss, backward pass, gradient descent loop.

title: Build a feedforward neural network with nn.Module: MNIST digit classification
description: Build a 3-layer MLP with nn.Module for MNIST. Use DataLoader, Adam optimizer, CrossEntropyLoss. Track training loss and val accuracy per epoch. Reach 97%+ accuracy.

title: CNNs with PyTorch: build LeNet-5 for CIFAR-10, apply batch norm and dropout
description: Build a LeNet-5 style CNN for CIFAR-10. Add BatchNorm and Dropout. Compare accuracy with/without. Use torchvision.transforms for data augmentation.

title: Transfer learning with a pretrained ResNet-18 on a custom image dataset
description: Use torchvision's ResNet-18 pretrained on ImageNet. Freeze backbone, replace head, fine-tune on a small Kaggle image dataset (e.g. Cats vs Dogs subset). Reach 95%+ accuracy.

title: Enrol and complete Module 1 of DeepLearning.AI Machine Learning Specialization
description: Enrol in the Andrew Ng ML Specialization on Coursera (audit for free). Complete week 1 and 2 of Course 1: supervised learning labs in Python.

title: Build Streamlit app wrapping your best ML model with a prediction form
description: Create a Streamlit app that loads your saved joblib model, shows a form for input features, and displays the prediction with a confidence bar. Deploy free on Streamlit Community Cloud.

resources.title: CampusX — Deploy ML Model with Streamlit

title: Complete DeepLearning.AI ML Specialization Course 1 (weeks 3–4 lab work)
description: Complete Course 1 labs: neural networks in NumPy from scratch, backprop implementation, binary classification network. Submit all graded assignments.

title: Recurrent neural networks: LSTM for time-series prediction with PyTorch
description: Build an LSTM that predicts the next 7 days of stock price (use yfinance for data). Evaluate with MAE. Plot predictions vs actuals.

title: Experiment tracking with MLflow: log params, metrics, and artifacts for your best model
description: Install MLflow. Wrap your best ML project training loop to log hyperparameters, metrics per epoch, and the final model artifact. View results in the MLflow UI.

title: Polish Streamlit app: add EDA charts tab, feature importance chart, model metrics panel
description: Extend your Streamlit app with tabs: Predictions, Data Explorer (5 charts from your EDA), and Model Info (SHAP summary plot, metrics table). Update the GitHub README with a live demo link.

title: Kaggle competition entry: submit your ML model to an active beginner competition
description: Join the Titanic or House Prices Kaggle competition (or another active one). Submit your best model predictions. Aim for top 40%. Document your approach in the notebook.

title: Data Scientist path wrap-up: push all projects to GitHub with polished READMEs
description: Ensure both projects (EDA notebook + Streamlit ML app) have GitHub repos with: demo link, screenshot, setup instructions, and a description of the approach. Add them to LinkedIn Featured section.

title: Month 2 Milestone: Live Streamlit app + Kaggle notebook + certificate progress 50%
description: Your Streamlit ML demo must be live. Your Kaggle competition submission must be in. You must be 50%+ through the DeepLearning.AI ML Specialization. Update LinkedIn with ML skills.

title: Anthropic Claude API quickstart: messages API, system prompts, streaming
description: Sign up for Anthropic API. Complete the quickstart. Build a Python script that sends a message, receives a streaming response, and calculates token cost. Try 3 different system prompts.

title: Prompt engineering patterns: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, role prompting
description: Work through the Anthropic prompt engineering guide. For each pattern, write a concrete example and measure output quality differences. Build a notebook comparing 4 prompting strategies on the same task.

title: OpenAI API: completions, function calling, structured outputs with Pydantic
description: Build a Python script using the OpenAI SDK that uses function calling to extract structured data (name, date, amount) from 10 invoice text samples. Validate output with Pydantic models.

title: Advanced prompt patterns: XML tags, constitutional AI, multi-turn conversation design
description: Study Anthropic's guide on XML tagging and constitutional prompting. Build a customer support bot with a multi-turn conversation loop, hard refusal instructions, and structured XML output.

title: Token economics: context windows, caching, batching — build a cost calculator
description: Study Anthropic and OpenAI pricing pages. Build a Python script that estimates cost for a given prompt+response across 5 models. Implement prompt caching with Anthropic's cache_control API.

resources.title: CampusX — LLM Token Economics & Cost Optimization

title: Build a multi-turn CLI chatbot with Claude: system prompt, memory, conversation history
description: Build a CLI chatbot that maintains conversation history in a Python list and sends it with each API call. Add a /clear command, a /summarize command that compresses the conversation, and a /save command.

title: Text embeddings: OpenAI and Sentence-Transformers — cosine similarity, semantic search
description: Generate embeddings for 100 Wikipedia sentences using both OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Implement cosine similarity search from scratch. Compare results.

title: ChromaDB: create a local vector store, upsert documents, query by similarity
description: Install ChromaDB. Embed 200 documents (use a Wikipedia dump or your own content), upsert into a Chroma collection, and build a semantic search function that returns top-5 with scores.

title: RAG from scratch: chunk → embed → store → retrieve → augment → generate
description: Build a minimal RAG pipeline in 150 lines of Python (no LangChain). Load a PDF, chunk by paragraphs, embed with sentence-transformers, store in Chroma, retrieve top-3 on query, generate answer with Claude.

title: LangChain fundamentals: chains, prompts, retrievers, memory, LCEL
description: Work through the LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) quickstart. Rebuild your RAG pipeline using LangChain's RetrievalQA chain. Add ConversationBufferMemory for multi-turn support.

title: Pinecone vector database: create index, upsert with metadata, filtered retrieval
description: Create a Pinecone account (free tier). Upsert your embedded documents with metadata (source, date, category). Test metadata filtering to retrieve only documents from a specific source.

title: Start DeepLearning.AI short course: LangChain for LLM Application Development
description: Complete the full free DeepLearning.AI course on LangChain (2–3 hours). Build the document Q&A app from the course. Add it to your GitHub.

title: Anthropic tool use: define tools, handle tool_use blocks, multi-turn tool calling
description: Build a Python agent that uses Anthropic's tool use API to answer questions by calling a web search tool (use Tavily or DuckDuckGo API). Handle multi-turn tool call loops correctly.

title: Build a ReAct agent from scratch: reason → act → observe loop without frameworks
description: Implement a ReAct agent loop in pure Python using Claude. Give it 3 tools: calculator, Wikipedia search, and current datetime. Trace each step with verbose logging.

resources.title: CampusX — Building AI Agents from Scratch

title: Advanced RAG: hybrid search (BM25 + vector), reranking with cross-encoder
description: Implement hybrid search: BM25 retrieval with rank_bm25 + vector retrieval with Chroma. Merge results with reciprocal rank fusion. Add a cross-encoder reranker with sentence-transformers.

title: Design and start building your RAG application: document Q&A on a domain you know
description: Pick a meaningful domain (your university notes, a public technical manual, legislation, etc.). Design the chunking strategy, embedding model, and retrieval approach. Set up the project repo.

title: LlamaIndex: document loaders, node parsers, query engines, and evaluation
description: Complete the LlamaIndex Starter Tutorial. Build a query engine over 5 PDFs. Evaluate retrieval quality with LlamaIndex's built-in evaluators (faithfulness, relevancy).

title: RAG app prototype: working end-to-end with a simple Gradio or Streamlit interface
description: Your RAG app must accept a question, retrieve relevant chunks, and generate a grounded answer with source citations. Deploy a working prototype on Streamlit Cloud or HuggingFace Spaces.

title: OpenAI Assistants API: file search, code interpreter, persistent threads
description: Build an assistant using the OpenAI Assistants API with file_search enabled on your RAG corpus. Test persistent thread memory across sessions. Compare output quality against your manual RAG.

title: Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP): build a custom MCP server with 3 tools
description: Study the MCP specification. Build a local MCP server in Python that exposes 3 tools: filesystem reader, database query, and web scraper. Test it with Claude Desktop.

title: Fine-tuning fundamentals: LoRA and QLoRA theory + run a fine-tuning job on OpenAI
description: Read the LoRA paper abstract and the HuggingFace PEFT docs. Run a fine-tuning job on OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) with 50 custom examples. Evaluate the fine-tuned model vs base.

title: Complete and polish RAG application: add evaluation scores, confidence display, citations
description: Finalize your RAG app: add per-answer faithfulness and relevancy scores from RAGAS, show retrieved chunks as expandable citations, handle no-answer gracefully. Write a comprehensive README.

title: Deploy RAG app to production: Vercel (Next.js frontend) + Railway/Render (FastAPI backend)
description: Build a minimal Next.js frontend for your RAG app. Deploy FastAPI backend on Railway free tier. Connect frontend to API. Add the live URL to your GitHub README and LinkedIn.

resources.title: CampusX — Deploying AI Apps to Production

title: Build and deploy agent project: web research agent with tool use, deployed on HF Spaces
description: Build a web research agent using Claude + tool use: it takes a research question, searches the web, reads 3 sources, and writes a structured report. Deploy on HuggingFace Spaces with Gradio.

title: Month 3 Milestone: 2 deployed AI projects live + AWS AI Practitioner exam booked
description: Both your RAG app and agent project must be deployed with public URLs. AWS AI Practitioner exam must be scheduled. Update LinkedIn with GenAI skills: LLM APIs, RAG, agents, vector databases.

title: LLM evaluation with RAGAS: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall
description: Run RAGAS evaluation on your RAG app with a test set of 20 Q&A pairs. Compute faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. Identify and fix the weakest metric.

title: HuggingFace Transformers: load, tokenize, run inference, and push a model to the Hub
description: Load BERT and GPT-2 with the Transformers library. Run inference on 10 text samples. Fine-tune GPT-2 on 100 custom sentences using Trainer API. Push the fine-tuned model to HuggingFace Hub.

title: Vercel AI SDK: streaming chat UI in Next.js with useChat hook and server actions
description: Build a streaming chat UI using Vercel AI SDK with useChat. Connect to Claude via the Anthropic provider. Add a system prompt selector with 3 personas. Deploy to Vercel.

resources.title: CampusX — Building Chat Interfaces with LLMs

title: AWS AI Practitioner exam prep: 60 practice questions + review weak areas
description: Complete 60 AWS practice questions from AWS Skill Builder or Whizlabs. Score per domain. Review any domain below 70%. Read the AWS AI/ML service overview whitepapers for weak areas.

title: System design for AI apps: stateless APIs, async queues, caching layers, rate limiting
description: Study the AI system design primer. Design the architecture for your RAG app at 1000 concurrent users: identify bottlenecks, add Redis caching for embeddings, describe a job queue for slow requests.

resources.title: CampusX — System Design for ML/AI Applications

title: Containerize your RAG FastAPI backend with Docker and docker-compose
description: Write a Dockerfile for your FastAPI backend. Write a docker-compose.yml with the app + a Redis container. Verify the app starts cleanly with docker-compose up. Add Makefile targets for build/up/down.

title: GitHub Actions CI: run tests and linting on every PR for your RAG project
description: Write a .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs pytest, ruff linter, and mypy type checker on every push to main. Add a status badge to your README. Fix any linting errors surfaced.

title: API design for AI services: REST conventions, error schemas, versioning, OpenAPI spec
description: Refactor your FastAPI backend to follow REST conventions. Add Pydantic error schemas, a /health endpoint, API versioning (v1/). Auto-generate OpenAPI spec and verify it with swagger-ui.

title: Observability: add structured logging, Sentry error tracking, and basic metrics to your app
description: Add structlog for structured JSON logging to your FastAPI app. Integrate Sentry SDK for error tracking (free tier). Add a Prometheus-compatible /metrics endpoint using prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator.

title: Build your portfolio site: Next.js 14 with 4 project cards, about section, and contact form
description: Build a personal portfolio site using Next.js 14 App Router. Include: hero section, about, 4 project cards (your 4 projects), skills section, and a contact form (use Resend or Formspree). Deploy to Vercel.

title: Write your AI Engineer resume: 1-page format, quantified achievements, ATS-optimized
description: Write your resume using the XYZ format (Accomplished X as measured by Y by doing Z). Include your 4 projects with live links and metrics. Scan with an ATS checker (Jobscan or Resume Worded).

resources.title: CampusX — Data Science / AI Resume Tips

title: LinkedIn profile overhaul: headline, about, experience, featured projects, skills
description: Rewrite your LinkedIn headline to include target role and top skills. Write a 3-paragraph About section. Update all experience with quantified bullets. Add all 4 projects to Featured. Request 3 endorsements.

resources.title: CampusX — LinkedIn & Job Hunting for Data Scientists

title: DSA day 1: arrays and strings — solve 2 LeetCode easy/medium problems
description: Solve Two Sum (LC #1) and Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters (LC #3). Time yourself to 30 min each. Write your approach and time complexity in a comment before coding.

title: Naukri profile setup: headline, skills, resume upload, job alerts for AI roles in India
description: Create or update your Naukri.com profile. Upload your polished resume. Set job alerts for: AI Engineer, ML Engineer, Data Scientist in Bangalore/Hyderabad/Remote. Apply to 3 matching roles.

resources.title: CampusX — Job Hunting for Data Scientists in India

title: DSA day 2: linked lists — solve Reverse Linked List (LC #206) and Merge Two Sorted Lists (LC #21)
description: Solve both problems iteratively first, then recursively. Draw the pointer diagrams before coding. Review solutions on NeetCode after.

title: Indeed and Wellfound (EU/Ireland focus): create profiles and apply to 3 roles each
description: Create profiles on Indeed and Wellfound. On Wellfound, fill out your AI Engineer profile completely (it's used by startups heavily in EU/Ireland). Apply to 3 matching roles on each platform.

title: DSA day 3: trees — Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (LC #102) and Maximum Depth (LC #104)
description: Implement BFS level-order traversal using a deque. Implement recursive and iterative DFS for max depth. Explain time/space complexity for both.

title: Mock interview session 1: 45-min technical interview with a peer or on Pramp
description: Book a mock interview on Pramp (free) or with a peer. 45 minutes: one DSA problem + one ML/AI system design question. Record it. Review the recording and note 3 areas to improve.

title: LinkedIn outreach: send 10 connection requests to AI engineers and 3 cold messages
description: Identify 10 AI Engineers or ML Engineers at target companies on LinkedIn. Send personalized connection requests (note: mention something specific about their work). Send 3 cold messages to recruiters at top target companies.

title: DSA day 4: dynamic programming — Climbing Stairs (LC #70) and Coin Change (LC #322)
description: Solve both with top-down memoization first, then bottom-up tabulation. Draw the DP table for Coin Change. Write the recurrence relation explicitly.

title: Behavioral interview prep: STAR stories for top 10 interview questions
description: Write STAR format answers for: Tell me about yourself, biggest challenge, conflict with a teammate, a project you're proud of, a failure and what you learned, why AI Engineering, how you stay current, a time you had to learn fast, leadership example, and your biggest weakness.

title: DSA day 5: graphs — Number of Islands (LC #200) and Clone Graph (LC #133)
description: Solve Number of Islands with both DFS and BFS. Solve Clone Graph iteratively. Discuss when to prefer DFS vs BFS for graph problems.

title: AI system design interview prep: design a RAG system, a recommendation engine, and a fraud detector
description: Write 1-page design documents for each system. For RAG: address chunking strategy, embedding model choice, retrieval, generation, evaluation. Practice explaining each design out loud in 10 minutes.

title: Mock interview session 2 + review all applications and follow up on any pending
description: Do a second Pramp mock interview. Review all job applications submitted — follow up via email on any applied 2+ weeks ago. Update your job tracker in this app.

title: Final portfolio review: all 4 projects live, portfolio site deployed, resume v2 complete
description: Verify all 4 projects are live with public URLs. Portfolio site deployed on Vercel. Resume scored 80+ on Resume Worded. LinkedIn profile strength: All-Star. Everything links to everything.

title: Apply to 5 senior target companies and write custom cover letters for each
description: Identify your top 5 target companies (mix of product and services companies, India + EU options). Write tailored cover letters referencing their specific AI work. Apply via LinkedIn Easy Apply + direct company career pages.

resources.title: CampusX — Job Hunting Strategy for AI Roles

title: Month 4 Milestone: AWS cert earned + 20+ applications submitted + first interview scheduled
description: AWS AI Practitioner certificate must be earned and uploaded to LinkedIn. Minimum 20 job applications submitted across LinkedIn/Naukri/Indeed/Wellfound. At least 1 interview or screening call scheduled.
